title: Exercise class 5: ius gentium, sovereignty, public law up to the 19th century

5.title: Aquinas's four grades of law
5.text: To medieval natural law the exercise class gives a concrete structure worth being able to list from the top down. THOMAS AQUINAS (1225–1274) builds a HIERARCHY OF 'LAWS' IN FOUR GRADES. (1) LEX AETERNA, THE ETERNAL LAW — the highest; IT IS BEYOND HUMAN GRASP, because God is the 'UNCAUSED CAUSE' of everything. It is the order by which the world is established. (2) LEX DIVINA, THE DIVINE LAW — the one pronounced in HOLY SCRIPTURE, that is, revealed. (3) LEX NATURALIS, NATURAL LAW — THE LAW MAN DECIPHERS BY REASON AND WHICH IS DERIVED FROM THE LEX AETERNA. It is that part of the eternal order man can reach on his own. (4) LEX HUMANA, HUMAN LAW — the law made by human beings. THE HIERARCHY IS AT ONCE A JUSTIFICATION AND A LIMIT: human law is valid because it rests on a higher grade, and it is invalid where it contradicts it. The idea is that THERE ARE LAWS AND PRINCIPLES THAT EXIST IN THE WORLD BY NATURE, NOT BECAUSE HUMAN BEINGS MADE THEM. In the Middle Ages, then, natural law HAS A DIVINE COMPONENT — and it is precisely that component Grotius will later remove.

terms.def: Aquinas's four grades: the eternal law (beyond grasp), the revealed, the one deciphered by reason, and the human.

cards.q: Which four grades of law does Thomas Aquinas distinguish?
cards.a: 1) LEX AETERNA, THE ETERNAL LAW — the highest, BEYOND HUMAN GRASP (God as the 'uncaused cause'). 2) LEX DIVINA — THE DIVINE LAW pronounced in SCRIPTURE. 3) LEX NATURALIS — the law MAN DECIPHERS BY REASON, derived from the lex aeterna. 4) LEX HUMANA — the law made by human beings. The hierarchy is at once a JUSTIFICATION AND A LIMIT of human law.

6.title: Who made up the Western community of international law
6.text: The exercise class answers the question BETWEEN WHOM the ius gentium actually applied, and the list is more surprising than one would expect. THE WESTERN COMMUNITY OF INTERNATIONAL LAW consisted of the GREAT CHRISTIAN KINGDOMS AS INDIVIDUAL (SOVEREIGN) STATES — FRANCE, ENGLAND, THE IBERIAN KINGDOMS (Castile, Aragon and Portugal), POLAND, DENMARK, SICILY and of course the ROMAN-GERMAN EMPIRE — AND IN ADDITION THE TEUTONIC ORDER AND THE ORDER OF MALTA. That is: TWO KNIGHTLY ORDERS STOOD IN THIS COMMUNITY ALONGSIDE KINGDOMS. This is good evidence that subjectivity was then derived not from territory and population as it is today, but from POSITION WITHIN THE CHRISTIAN ORDER — which is why an order without a land of its own could be an equal participant. (The Order of Malta, incidentally, still has a special status in international law and maintains diplomatic relations.)

cards.q: Who made up the Western community of international law in the late Middle Ages?
cards.a: The GREAT CHRISTIAN KINGDOMS as sovereign states — FRANCE, ENGLAND, THE IBERIAN KINGDOMS, POLAND, DENMARK, SICILY, THE ROMAN-GERMAN EMPIRE — AND IN ADDITION THE TEUTONIC ORDER AND THE ORDER OF MALTA. Two knightly orders therefore stood alongside kingdoms: subjectivity derived not from territory but from POSITION WITHIN THE CHRISTIAN ORDER.

8.title: The Spanish era: how the ius gentium became a science
8.text: DURING THE SPANISH ERA (1500–1648) THE IUS GENTIUM AND THE IUS NATURAE SLOWLY BEGAN TO TURN INTO A SCIENCE AND INTO INDEPENDENT LEGAL DISCIPLINES. The exercise class names the COMPONENTS that made this possible. (a) LATE SPANISH SCHOLASTICISM: FRANCISCO SUÁREZ (1548–1617) distinguished TWO FORMS OF THE IUS GENTIUM — 'IUS GENTIUM INTER SE', that is, IUS INTER GENTES or the LAW BETWEEN NATIONS (external law), and 'IUS GENTIUM INTRA SE', that is, INTERNAL LAW. For the first time this separates what we today call international law from the general principles applying within states. (b) POLITICAL THEORY, which emerged as an independent discipline — its foundation was laid by MACHIAVELLI. To this belongs, from the earlier sections, BODIN'S DOCTRINE OF SOVEREIGNTY. THE FRAME OF THE ERA: in the Empire the PEACE OF AUGSBURG (1555) with the principle 'CUIUS REGIO, EIUS RELIGIO' — the exercise calls it the FIRST STEP ON THE ROAD TO A EUROPEAN SYSTEM OF SOVEREIGN STATES; then the THIRTY YEARS' WAR and the PEACE OF WESTPHALIA (1648), which ends the religious wars in the Empire. THE CONSEQUENCES OF THE PEACE OF WESTPHALIA: THE EMPIRE LOSES POWER BECAUSE THE GREAT PRINCIPALITIES GAIN GREATER SOVEREIGNTY, and FRANCE OVERTAKES SPANISH PREDOMINANCE IN EUROPE — with which the FRENCH ERA begins.

terms.term: ius gentium inter se × intra se
terms.def: Suárez's distinction: the law between nations (external) × internal law.

cards.q: How did Suárez distinguish the two forms of the ius gentium, and why does it matter?
cards.a: 'IUS GENTIUM INTER SE' = IUS INTER GENTES, THE LAW BETWEEN NATIONS (external), and 'IUS GENTIUM INTRA SE' = INTERNAL LAW. For the first time this SEPARATES WHAT WE TODAY CALL INTERNATIONAL LAW from the general principles applying within states.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Why is the Peace of Augsburg the first step towards a system of sovereign states?
cards.a: Because by the principle 'CUIUS REGIO, EIUS RELIGIO' (1555) it granted the TERRITORIAL LORD THE RIGHT TO DECIDE ON RELIGION — recognizing his power in a field hitherto governed by the universal church. The PEACE OF WESTPHALIA (1648) completed it: THE EMPIRE LOST POWER because THE GREAT PRINCIPALITIES GAINED GREATER SOVEREIGNTY, and FRANCE OVERTOOK SPANISH PREDOMINANCE — the FRENCH ERA begins.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

10.title: The French era: from divine law to reason and the domestic analogy
10.text: IN THE 17TH CENTURY THE IUS GENTIUM BEGINS TO BE CALLED THE 'LAW OF NATIONS' — the term was introduced by RICHARD ZOUCHE. This law of nations is governed by MODERN NATURAL-LAW THINKING, WHICH HAS CAST OFF ITS RELIGIOUS TIES AND TURNED INTO A LAW OF REASON — the principal name is SAMUEL PUFENDORF. A SHIFT WITHIN NATURAL LAW worth remembering: THE OLDER THEORIES OF THE LAW OF REASON ASSUMED THAT NATURAL LAW, LIKE HUMAN REASON, IS UNCHANGING AND MUST THEREFORE REMAIN IDENTICAL REGARDLESS OF TIME AND PLACE (the absolute law of reason). IN THE 18TH CENTURY, HOWEVER, THE IDEA GAINS GROUND THAT NATURAL LAW MAY TAKE DIFFERENT FORMS ACCORDING TO TIME AND PLACE. In the 18th century the ius gentium is determined by a SYNTHESIS OF NATURAL LAW AND THE ENLIGHTENMENT, and THOMAS RUTHERFORD (1756) sums it up in a sentence worth knowing: 'THE LAW OF NATIONS IS ONLY THE LAW OF NATURE APPLIED TO THE COLLECTIVE PERSONS OF CIVIL SOCIETIES.' From this follows the 'DOMESTIC ANALOGY': THE PARALLEL BETWEEN THE INDIVIDUAL AND THE INDIVIDUAL STATE. JUST AS THE INDIVIDUAL HAS CERTAIN INALIENABLE RIGHTS, SO THE STATE TOO POSSESSES 'ABSOLUTE NATURAL RIGHTS' FLOWING FROM ITS NATURE — THE RIGHT TO EXISTENCE AND SELF-PRESERVATION, THE RIGHT TO INDEPENDENCE AND SOVEREIGNTY, THE RIGHT TO EQUALITY. And the ius gentium will finally become INTERNATIONAL LAW, a term coined by the British positivist JEREMY BENTHAM (1748–1832).

terms.def: The state has 'absolute natural rights' analogously to the individual — to existence, independence and equality.

cards.q: Who introduced the term 'law of nations' and what governed it?
cards.a: RICHARD ZOUCHE in the 17th century. This law of nations was governed by MODERN NATURAL-LAW THINKING, WHICH HAD CAST OFF ITS RELIGIOUS TIES AND TURNED INTO A LAW OF REASON — the principal name is SAMUEL PUFENDORF.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: What shift took place within natural law in the 18th century?
cards.a: THE OLDER THEORIES assumed that natural law, like human reason, is UNCHANGING and must therefore remain IDENTICAL REGARDLESS OF TIME AND PLACE (the absolute law of reason). IN THE 18TH CENTURY THE IDEA GAINS GROUND THAT IT MAY TAKE DIFFERENT FORMS ACCORDING TO TIME AND PLACE.

cards.q: What is the 'domestic analogy' and which rights does it give the state?
cards.a: THE PARALLEL BETWEEN THE INDIVIDUAL AND THE INDIVIDUAL STATE, expressed by Rutherford (1756): 'THE LAW OF NATIONS IS ONLY THE LAW OF NATURE APPLIED TO THE COLLECTIVE PERSONS OF CIVIL SOCIETIES.' Like the individual, THE STATE TOO HAS 'ABSOLUTE NATURAL RIGHTS': THE RIGHT TO EXISTENCE AND SELF-PRESERVATION, TO INDEPENDENCE AND SOVEREIGNTY, TO EQUALITY.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

11.title: The English era 1815–1914
11.text: The exercise class divides the history of international law into ERAS BY LEADING POWER — the SPANISH (1500–1648), the FRENCH (1648–1815), the ENGLISH (1815–1914) — and this is a useful skeleton, because the examiner asks about periods. THE ENGLISH ERA BEGINS WITH THE CONGRESS OF VIENNA (1814/15), which AIMS AT RESTORING THE 'OLD ORDER' AFTER THE FALL OF NAPOLEON. A SYSTEM OF ALLIANCES ACROSS EUROPE ARISES, DESIGNED TO ENSURE THAT ANY UPRISING, ESPECIALLY BY LIBERAL MOVEMENTS, IS IMMEDIATELY SUPPRESSED. THE 19TH CENTURY is marked by TWO OPPOSING MOVEMENTS: THE EMERGENCE OF NATION STATES AND THE STRUGGLE OF THE FORMER COLONIES IN AMERICA FOR INDEPENDENCE — connected with the RISE OF THE USA TO A REGIONAL POWER (the MONROE DOCTRINE 1823) — AND AT THE SAME TIME CONTINUING IMPERIALISM, ESPECIALLY IN AFRICA. That is: in Europe and America nations free themselves, in Africa they are subjugated. AND ONE DATE TO REMEMBER, BECAUSE IT SHOWS THE BOUNDARY OF THE 'CIVILIZED NATIONS': IN 1856 THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE BECOMES THE FIRST NON-CHRISTIAN MEMBER of the European community of international law (by the Treaty of Paris after the Crimean War).

cards.q: Into which eras does the exercise class divide the history of international law?
cards.a: The SPANISH (1500–1648), the FRENCH (1648–1815) and the ENGLISH (1815–1914) — by leading power.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: What characterizes the English era, and which date shows the boundary of the 'civilized nations'?
cards.a: It begins with the CONGRESS OF VIENNA (1814/15), which restores the 'OLD ORDER' and creates a SYSTEM OF ALLIANCES FOR THE IMMEDIATE SUPPRESSION OF LIBERAL MOVEMENTS. The 19th century has two opposing movements: THE EMERGENCE OF NATION STATES and the independence of the American colonies (the rise of the USA, the MONROE DOCTRINE 1823) — AND AT THE SAME TIME CONTINUING IMPERIALISM IN AFRICA. IN 1856 THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE BECOMES THE FIRST NON-CHRISTIAN MEMBER of the community.

12.title: Siyar: Islamic international law
12.text: The exercise class adds to the European series a counterpart that global legal history likes to ask about. SIYAR is, in Islamic law (FIQH), the BRANCH GOVERNING THE LAW OF WAR AND THE LAW OF FOREIGNERS. It is an INDEPENDENT BRANCH OF ISLAMIC LEGAL SCIENCE, derived from the QUR'AN, the SUNNA, IJMA and also from the LEGAL PROVISIONS ON JIHAD. It is defined thus: SIYAR IS THE BODY OF RULES DETERMINING THE ATTITUDE OF THE ISLAMIC STATE TOWARDS NON-MUSLIMS (DHIMMA). And the exercise assesses it as a PRECURSOR OF INTERNATIONAL LEGAL REGULATION GROUNDED IN THE LEGAL PRACTICE OF ISLAMIC EXPANSION. The comparison that follows is interesting: THE EUROPEAN IUS GENTIUM AROSE AMONG EQUAL CHRISTIAN RULERS; SIYAR, BY CONTRAST, GOVERNS THE RELATION OF ONE ORDER TO THOSE WHO DO NOT BELONG TO IT. Both are attempts to order relations across the boundary of one's own community — only from opposite sides.

terms.def: The branch of Islamic legal science governing the law of war and the law of foreigners — the attitude of the Islamic state towards non-Muslims.

cards.q: What is siyar and what is it derived from?
cards.a: The branch of Islamic legal science (FIQH) governing the LAW OF WAR AND THE LAW OF FOREIGNERS; it is derived from the QUR'AN, the SUNNA, IJMA and the provisions on JIHAD. It is the BODY OF RULES DETERMINING THE ATTITUDE OF THE ISLAMIC STATE TOWARDS NON-MUSLIMS (DHIMMA) and is regarded as a PRECURSOR OF INTERNATIONAL LEGAL REGULATION grounded in the practice of Islamic expansion.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

cards.q: How does siyar differ from the European ius gentium?
cards.a: THE EUROPEAN IUS GENTIUM AROSE AMONG EQUAL CHRISTIAN RULERS; SIYAR, BY CONTRAST, GOVERNS THE RELATION OF ONE ORDER TO THOSE WHO DO NOT BELONG TO IT. Both are attempts to order relations across the boundary of one's own community — only from opposite sides.
cards.topic: Ancient Legal Cultures; History of Islamic Law

16.title: Why public law was transformed in the 16th and 17th centuries
16.text: The exercise class gives the CAUSES, and for this question they are more valuable than a description. THE REASONS FOR THE CHANGES: FROM THE 14TH CENTURY, STATE-BUILDING AND THE CENTRALIZATION OF POWER; FROM THE 15TH TO THE 17TH CENTURY, INNOVATIONS — TECHNOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, MILITARY AND FINANCIAL — further EUROPEAN EXPANSION (the discovery of America) and the REFORMATION. To these is added JEAN BODIN AND HIS DOCTRINE OF SOVEREIGNTY. AND THE RESULT: WITH THE EMERGENCE OF 'STATES' AND THE DOGMA OF SOVEREIGNTY THE IUS PUBLICUM TURNS INTO STATE LAW. ABSOLUTISM: THE RULER AS SOLE LEGISLATOR — 'L'ÉTAT, C'EST MOI'. And one Austrian note that comes in useful: IN ABSOLUTIST 18TH-CENTURY AUSTRIA ADMINISTRATIVE LAW DEVELOPS AS AN INDEPENDENT BRANCH. At the same time, alongside constitutional law and the ius publicum in the narrower sense, TWO FURTHER DISCIPLINES establish themselves in the course of the 17TH CENTURY that can be counted as public law in the broader sense: NATURAL LAW AND (EUROPEAN) INTERNATIONAL LAW.

cards.q: Which causes transformed public law in the 16th and 17th centuries?
cards.a: FROM THE 14TH CENTURY, STATE-BUILDING AND THE CENTRALIZATION OF POWER; FROM THE 15TH–17TH CENTURY, TECHNOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, MILITARY AND FINANCIAL INNOVATIONS; EUROPEAN EXPANSION and the REFORMATION; and BODIN'S DOCTRINE OF SOVEREIGNTY. The result: WITH THE EMERGENCE OF STATES AND THE DOGMA OF SOVEREIGNTY THE IUS PUBLICUM TURNS INTO STATE LAW.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Which two disciplines established themselves alongside constitutional law in the 17th century?
cards.a: NATURAL LAW and (EUROPEAN) INTERNATIONAL LAW — counted as public law in the broader sense. (In absolutist 18th-century Austria ADMINISTRATIVE LAW is added as an independent branch.)
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

18.title: The Peace of Westphalia: two treaties and one paradox
18.text: To the Peace of Westphalia the exercise class adds precisions that can earn a point in the exam. THERE ARE TWO PEACE TREATIES signed in 1648 in two Westphalian towns: AT OSNABRÜCK BETWEEN THE EMPIRE AND SWEDEN and AT MÜNSTER BETWEEN THE EMPIRE AND FRANCE. (The reason for the double negotiation was practical: the Protestant and Catholic sides would not sit down at one table.) AND A PARADOX THE EXERCISE STATES EXPRESSLY: ALTHOUGH FRANCE WAS CATHOLIC, IT FOUGHT ON THE SIDE OF THE PROTESTANT UNION — WHILE AT HOME, UNDER LOUIS XIV, PROTESTANTS WERE RUTHLESSLY PERSECUTED. It is the best evidence that the religious war was waged for reasons of power, not of doctrine. THE CONCEPT OF SOVEREIGNTY APPEARS WITH THE PEACE OF WESTPHALIA AS AN INSTRUMENT FOR WARDING OFF ALL EXTERNAL INFLUENCES — and that is a precise definition: sovereignty here means not so much power inwards as a SHIELD AGAINST INTERFERENCE FROM OUTSIDE. THE CONSEQUENCE: THE EMPIRE LOSES POWER BECAUSE THE PRINCIPALITIES GAIN IT; and WITH THE PEACE OF WESTPHALIA THE RELIGIOUS WARS IN THE EMPIRE END AND THE RISE OF FRANCE BEGINS.

cards.q: What does the Peace of Westphalia consist of and why were there two places of negotiation?
cards.a: TWO TREATIES signed in 1648: AT OSNABRÜCK BETWEEN THE EMPIRE AND SWEDEN and AT MÜNSTER BETWEEN THE EMPIRE AND FRANCE. The reason was practical: THE PROTESTANT AND CATHOLIC SIDES WOULD NOT SIT DOWN AT ONE TABLE.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: What paradox does French participation in the Thirty Years' War show?
cards.a: ALTHOUGH FRANCE WAS CATHOLIC, IT FOUGHT ON THE SIDE OF THE PROTESTANT UNION — WHILE AT HOME, UNDER LOUIS XIV, PROTESTANTS WERE RUTHLESSLY PERSECUTED. It is the best evidence that the religious war was waged for reasons of POWER, not of doctrine.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: How does the exercise class define sovereignty in the Westphalian sense?
cards.a: As an INSTRUMENT FOR WARDING OFF ALL EXTERNAL INFLUENCES — sovereignty here means not so much power INWARDS as a SHIELD AGAINST INTERFERENCE FROM OUTSIDE. The consequence is that THE EMPIRE LOSES POWER because the PRINCIPALITIES gain it.

20.title: Absolutism where it succeeded and where it did not
20.text: The exercise class sets three cases side by side, and the contrast makes a good answer. THE DEFINITION: FROM THE 17TH CENTURY SOME RULERS SUCCEEDED IN OVERCOMING THE RULER–ESTATES DUALISM ENTIRELY and in making their rule 'DETACHED' (ABSOLUTUS) FROM THE ASSEMBLY OF THE ESTATES. THE ABSOLUTIST PRINCE BECOMES THE SOLE BEARER OF SOVEREIGNTY AND UNITES ALL STATE POWERS IN HIS PERSON — he is the SOLE LEGISLATOR AND THE SUPREME JUDGE. THE PROTOTYPE IS FRANCE UNDER LOUIS XIV, THE 'SUN KING' (1638–1715). IN ENGLAND THE ATTEMPT AT ABSOLUTISM FAILED: the BILL OF RIGHTS OF 1689 granted parliament far-reaching privileges, among them the RIGHT TO ENACT STATUTES — a CONSTITUTIONAL MONARCHY arose. Closely connected with this is JOHN LOCKE (1632–1704), who MODIFIED HOBBES'S THEORY OF THE SOCIAL CONTRACT: THE SOVEREIGN IS INSTITUTED FOR THE GOOD OF THE SUBJECTS, AND IF HE ABUSES HIS POWER THE PEOPLE HAVE A RIGHT OF RESISTANCE; to this belongs the idea of the SEPARATION OF POWERS. IN AUSTRIA, MARIA THERESA (1717–1780) is more or less a classic absolutist ruler and absolutism is at its height under her — BUT THE EXERCISE ADDS A NUANCE: BECAUSE OF HER DEEP PIETY HER CONCEPTION OF RULE WAS DIFFERENT. She felt responsible TO GOD ALONE, but PRECISELY FOR THAT REASON she saw herself as BOUND TO CARE FOR THE COMMON GOOD OF HER SUBJECTS. AND AN IMPORTANT NOTE: THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE ITSELF WAS NOT GOVERNED ABSOLUTISTICALLY — THERE THE EMPEROR–ESTATES DUALISM REMAINED.

cards.q: What does absolutism mean and who is its prototype?
cards.a: From the 17th century some rulers succeeded in OVERCOMING THE RULER–ESTATES DUALISM ENTIRELY and making their rule 'DETACHED' (ABSOLUTUS) from the assembly of the estates. The prince becomes the SOLE BEARER OF SOVEREIGNTY, unites all powers in his person and is the SOLE LEGISLATOR AND SUPREME JUDGE. The prototype is FRANCE UNDER LOUIS XIV (1638–1715).
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: Why did absolutism fail in England and how does that connect with Locke?
cards.a: The BILL OF RIGHTS OF 1689 granted parliament far-reaching privileges including the RIGHT TO ENACT STATUTES — a CONSTITUTIONAL MONARCHY arose. LOCKE (1632–1704) modified Hobbes's social contract: THE SOVEREIGN IS INSTITUTED FOR THE GOOD OF THE SUBJECTS, AND IF HE ABUSES HIS POWER THE PEOPLE HAVE A RIGHT OF RESISTANCE; to this belongs the SEPARATION OF POWERS.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism

cards.q: How did Maria Theresa differ from a classic absolutist, and how was the Empire governed?
cards.a: She was more or less a classic absolutist and absolutism was at its height under her, BUT because of her DEEP PIETY she felt responsible TO GOD ALONE — and PRECISELY FOR THAT REASON saw herself as BOUND TO CARE FOR THE COMMON GOOD OF HER SUBJECTS. THE HOLY ROMAN EMPIRE ITSELF WAS NOT GOVERNED ABSOLUTISTICALLY — there the EMPEROR–ESTATES DUALISM remained.
cards.topic: The Westphalian Order and Early Constitutionalism
